_comment: Journeys known to be RED on this branch, with the reason and the work that closes each.
THIS FILE FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. An entry does not silence a journey — the journey
still runs, still prints every failed assertion, and is still counted. What the entry does
is stop the exit code from blocking every other branch on a defect that is already known
and already stated. And a ledgered journey that goes GREEN fails the run, so an entry
cannot outlive its defect: whoever lands the fix is told, by name, to delete the line.
An entry is only legitimate with a `closed_by` that names real work and an `evidence` line
that says what was measured. A ledger entry written to make a suite green is the defect
this whole layer exists to catch, wearing the suite's own uniform.

TWO ENTRIES in `known_red` below. This sentence has now been wrong four times — it read `No entries.` after the first was added, `ONE ENTRY TODAY` after the second, `THREE ENTRIES` after two of the three were closed, and `ONE ENTRY: the-flow-window-follows-the-position` after two of those three were closed and before this one arrived — which is the register summarising itself wrongly, the one error this file cannot afford. Count the keys in `known_red`; do not trust this line.

The entry before it — `a-value-can-be-traced-to-its-origin` — was removed when the journey went green on real functionality: the recording's own source now reaches the engine's VFS, `ct/originChain` returns hops that are actually CLASSIFIED (2 of 6 on the Noir demo capture, kind=functionCall confidence=0.7), and the State pane offers the control on exactly those values. A recording that published no source offers no control and says why instead, which is the correct behaviour for it rather than a remaining gap.

AND IT WAS CHALLENGED A SECOND TIME, ON A FULL SELFTEST PASS THAT FOUND JOURNEY 07 RED ON `dev` WITH NO ENTRY HERE — the ledger and the tree disagreeing, with the ledger looking like the dangerous half because it is what stops anyone looking. IT WAS THE TREE'S READING THAT WAS WRONG, AND THIS PARAGRAPH IS CORRECT AS WRITTEN. Measured at `8d1efe1a` over one tree, one bundle and one corpus, changing only the replay engine: on wasm `cf79c4bf9854465b…` the whole suite is 488 assertions, 22 GREEN, 0 red, 1 ledgered red, `RESULT: OK`, with journey 07 green at 2 of 6 hops classified over 6 values — the very numbers the paragraph above records. On wasm `3009b9892fa181cf…`, what the publisher was serving that day, ELEVEN journeys are red and journey 07 asks about 0 values. The engine cannot open half this corpus: `CTFS from_bytes failed for "trace/trace.ct": new-format container advertises steps.dat but no seekable step stream could be opened`. Every Noir recording here is a `C0DE72ACE2 04 0001` container and every chain capture is `C0DE72ACE2 03 0000`; the engine reads the second and rejects the first. AN ENTRY WRITTEN FOR THAT RED WOULD HAVE BEEN FALSE, and the both-directions rule would have failed the run the next time a working engine was staged — which is exactly what this file's previous paragraph says about the previous challenge, arriving a second time through a different door. THE STANDING RULE, NOW TWICE PAID FOR: before writing an entry for a journey that drives a session, READ THE ENGINE HASH `run.mjs` PRINTS. `run.mjs`'s Arm II now refuses to judge at all when the staged engine cannot open the corpus, so this particular reading can no longer be taken.

THAT REMOVAL WAS CHALLENGED AND IS CORRECT, and the challenge is worth recording because it was RIGHT ABOUT A RED and WRONG ABOUT WHICH ONE. `a-value-can-be-traced-to-its-origin` was reported red four times, reproduced locally each time. Re-measured here at 4419c61 on a fresh build: GREEN, 21 of 21 — and green again on a build carrying the PREVIOUS day's replay engine, so the unpinned engine is not a discriminator for it either. An entry restored for it would have been false, and the both-directions rule would have failed the run for a journey that passes.

The reproductions were real. The three failing assertions all four runs saw belong to `a-stepped-session-shows-the-values-it-is-at`, which WAS red, WAS un-ledgered, and stayed that way for three commits. Two journeys, one fingerprint, and the name travelled while the evidence did not. Anyone carrying a red between agents should carry the ASSERTION TEXT, not the journey name: `run.mjs --json` writes both.

WHY IT HID, since no entry ever described it and the next one of these will look the same. Its cause was `of tkInt: ""` in `client/hydrate/live_locals.nim` — the `replace` side of THIS SUITE'S OWN arm `L/the-value-kind-is-misread`, planted by a selftest run that never reached its restore step and then carried into a commit about the code pane, whose message says 'neither of them a behaviour change'. Three consequences worth naming: every integer local rendered as the empty string, which is what the three assertions were counting; the arm written to catch exactly this could no longer run, because its `find` is the ORIGINAL line and the mutation was already in the tree; and it did not reproduce on the deployed sites, because `live` and `staging` are both at `d57ae43`, three commits behind, where all 12 journeys are green. A deployed reading and a local reading disagreed and BOTH WERE RIGHT ABOUT THEIR OWN TREE.

It is fixed rather than ledgered. A ledger entry is for a defect that is stated and open; a one-token restore is not one, and an entry written instead of that restore is the entry this file's own rules refuse. Run the selftest from a THROWAWAY checkout: it edits real product source, and this is what a run that dies before step 4 costs.

the-flow-window-follows-the-position.reason:
THREE assertions are red, all three of them ONE sentence of `Omniscience-Flow.md`: "The declared extent is the source range of the function the window is over, and it contains every line the window draws. `functionFirst` is a 1-based source line, never `0` and never a sentinel." Measured over sixteen answers on the staged engine: every one is `fn=main first=0 last=15` over a window drawing lines 1..37, so the field is a sentinel AND the extent contains nothing it draws. The screen half is a separate record from the wire half deliberately — the wire counts the positions the ANSWER carried and the screen counts the lines the PANE drew, and a pane that drew a subset would satisfy one and not the other.

FOUR ASSERTIONS THAT USED TO BE RED HERE ARE GONE, AND THE SPEC REMOVED THEM RATHER THAN A MEASUREMENT. They demanded a window located at a position the session asked about, a window that changed on every step, and an overlay confined to the function the page says the session is in. The same section answers all three against them: the window is over the ENCLOSING CALL, positioned at that call's ENTRY step; "`rrTicks == 0` on a flow update is a legitimate value"; and "the window draws the entry line … a window whose extent looks wrong must be fixed AT THE FIELD, never by narrowing what the overlay draws". The first of them was asking for codetracer #606 back — the defect `e9242df3` removed when it restored full-call scope. Their replacements are the readings the same section prescribes, and they are GREEN on this build, which is the point: the capability the journey was written to defend is present.
the-flow-window-follows-the-position.cause:
THE ENGINE'S BUILD, NOT ITS SOURCE — which is why the fix that exists does not reach this, and why every earlier cause written here missed it.

codetracer `f2ac6ed5d` ("fix(flow,shortcuts): the window extent describes the window", 2026-09-03, on `dev` and on `cloud`) re-derives the extent from tree-sitter and is exactly the fix this needs. THE STAGED WASM CARRIES IT. Proven rather than inferred: that commit's re-derivation is the only caller of `get_first_last_fn_lines` on the flow path, and the engine's own log shows the call arriving there — `get_first_last_fn_lines "/private/tmp/blocktracer-fixture-rec/noir_space_ship/src/main.nr":12` followed by `result -1 -1` — once per window, sixteen times.

It answers `-1 -1` because `FileInfo.functions` is EMPTY, and it is empty because `db-backend`'s `syntax-highlight` feature is off in a wasm build. `Cargo.toml` says why in its own words: "Disable for WASM builds where the C grammars cannot be cross-compiled." `ExprLoader::load_file` therefore takes its `#[cfg(not(feature = "syntax-highlight"))]` arm — the engine logs `info for "src/main.nr" loaded (no syntax highlighting)`, which is that arm and no other — and never calls `parse_file`/`process_file`. `f2ac6ed5d`'s guard `ts_first > 0` then keeps the trace-record values, which for a Noir recording are `function_first = 0` (the recorder emits the declaration line as 0) and a `function_last` heuristic that ends at the first callee.

TWO THINGS THIS RULES OUT, both of which previous entries here spent effort on. The VFS key-spelling work — writing the bare path and the joined one — cannot help: with `functions` empty, no spelling finds anything. And `f2ac6ed5d`'s own gate, `src/db-backend/tests/flow_window_extent_test.rs`, is a native test, so it passes on a build that has the grammars while the build this product loads has none — a gate that cannot bite on the artefact the defect is in.
the-flow-window-follows-the-position.closed_by: In codetracer, and NOT closable from this repository: nothing in BlockTracer decides what extent the engine declares. Either the wasm build gains a source of function ranges that does not need the C grammars, or `FlowPreloader` derives the extent from something the wasm build has. Whichever is chosen, the gate has to run on a WASM build — the existing `flow_window_extent_test.rs` is native and is green today over exactly this defect. Then re-run this journey against an engine carrying it and delete this entry; the run will demand the deletion by name.

Eight moves — four `step-forward`, four `step-in` — over the noir_space_ship session, with the worker wrapped by an `addInitScript` before the page's own scripts ran.
  wire: 8 requests carrying 8 distinct ticks; 16 answers, all `t=0 fn=main first=0 last=15`, each drawing lines 1..37.

THE WALK STAYED INSIDE ONE CALL, which is why the two "it must change" assertions counted 1 and why they were never product facts. A DISCIPLINE NOTE that has now been paid for twice: both superseded entries here were written from readings that were correct about every number they quoted and wrong about what the numbers meant, because the walk they were measured over never left the frame. Carry the assertion text, not the journey name, and walk far enough to leave the call.

a-partly-positioned-recording-says-where.reason:
THREE assertions are red, and the detail line is the whole finding: `224 rows on screen, no mark, no position head and no note — the session is at step 0 of 459 and nothing on the page says so`.

`Source-Resolution.md` §7's last row is the clause, and it names this state exactly: "Partial source coverage | Source-level stepping where sources exist, instruction-level elsewhere, with the boundary visible in the source pane rather than silent". `Debugger-Integration.md` §5 says the same from the other side — "A single transaction routinely mixes both. The debugger must handle this without ceremony — it is the normal case, not an edge case" — and requires the transition to be visible.

THE SUBJECT IS THE FIRST RECORDING THIS TREE PUBLISHES THAT SEPARATES THE TWO FIDELITIES. `aztec-testnet-frames/0x0a807e4e…` runs 459 steps across TWO contracts: `0x…0003` positions 86 of its 108 steps, and `0x2fcd3dd5…` — steps 108..458 — positions none, because no distributor could prove its artifact. Its unpositioned runs are ticks 0..13, 27..34 and 108..458, measured from the published `positions/` sidecar. So 373 of 459 steps have no source line, and the page publishes no instruction listing to have a row for them.

WHY THE PAGE HAS NEITHER. `ssr.nim`'s Code-pane ladder is a CONTEST, not a union: `withPublishedSources` beats `withSourcePositions` beats `withInstructionListing`, the winner takes the pane, and `withInstructionListing` refuses outright any pane that is not `srcUnverified` or that already has documents. The middle rung wins here, so the pane is 32 Noir documents and nothing else. `SourceAvailabilityView` is one value for the whole session; the recording is not.

THE STATIC EXPORT IS SPARED BY AN ACCIDENT AND THAT IS WORTH SAYING, because it is why journey 02 is green over the same page. `demo_session.withSourceIsland` carries a landing rule in its own words — "a page may not report a position it is not showing" — and moves the served step to one there IS source for, landing this recording on 107, the LAST positioned step it has. Hydration has no counterpart: `run-to-entry` parks at tick 0, `positionDocumentIndex` correctly finds no published document for the engine's `/aztec/<txHash>.avm`, `decodeSourceIsland` clears `currentLine`, and nothing says why. Not a path-matching defect — the join is right and the file genuinely is not there.
a-partly-positioned-recording-says-where.cause:
ONE CAUSE, TWO PLACES, AND NEITHER IS A BUG IN A LINE. The product models source fidelity as a per-RECORDING boolean and this recording's is per-STEP.

  * `tools/chain/derive-instructions.mjs` REFUSES a container that positions any step, and     its reasoning is correct as far as it goes: on a positioned step the container spends     the `Step.line` field on the source line, so there is no program counter to publish and     both alternatives — a null in the column, or the line number — would be "a listing     that reads as a pc and is not one". What does not follow is refusing the WHOLE     container: 373 of these 459 steps do carry a pc, and they are exactly the steps with no     source line.
  * `client/src/ssr.nim`'s ladder then has nothing to fall back to, and would refuse it     anyway.

THE HYDRATED HALF IS DOWNSTREAM OF BOTH. `session_project.projectEditor`'s `savVerified` branch has one answer for an unresolvable position — clear the mark — and no second one.
a-partly-positioned-recording-says-where.closed_by:
FOUR EDITS, IN THIS ORDER, ALL IN THIS REPOSITORY.

1. `derive-instructions.mjs`: publish a listing for a partly-positioned container. Real    program counters at `path_id == 0` and a sentinel (`-1`, impossible as a bytecode    offset) at the rest — never a line number wearing a pc's column. The op/gas/context    columns are already complete on every step (REGISTERS.md measured 459 of 459), so only    `pc` is sparse. Keep the refusal for a container that positions EVERY step: that one    genuinely has no listing.
2. `instruction_listing.nim`: skip sentinel rows in `hexWidth`, `destinationSuffix` and    `explainsProgramCounters` — the last matters, because a sentinel differenced against a    real pc would refuse the opcode table for the whole recording.
3. `ssr.nim`: make the ladder a UNION for this class. The listing document joins the source    documents rather than competing with them, and the pane's header says which rung the    position is on — which is §5's "visible transition" and §7's "rather than silent".
4. `session_project.projectEditor`: when `positionDocumentIndex` resolves nothing, mark the    listing row at `rrTicks`. Row n IS tick n, so the join is the identity.

AND ONE HARNESS EDIT THAT MUST LAND WITH THEM, or three other journeys change subject silently: `tools/journeys/lib/corpus.mjs`'s `hasSource` reads `class="srcline" && !class="src instr"`, so a page holding BOTH kinds of document would classify as "no source" — moving this transaction into journey 10's subject set and out of journey 07's. It has to become "holds at least one source document".

Measured 2026-09-05 in worktree `bt-frames-reds`, branched from origin/dev 8d9a5834f37ba1c030f2d4353e6f95d12068084f, over `client/dist` built by `just export-hydrated` with the engine pinned by `client/hydrate/engine-pin.txt` (`pkg/db_backend_bg.wasm` sha256 22acb8e1ccf2d7aa0660143e78ad26088d61ec3c8168c28d57306715c37c685e, 18,117,658 bytes).

  live:                   step 0/459, 224 rows on screen, 0 marked, no `.srcpos` head, no `.srcnone` note. Eight live controls, phase=ready, zero uncaught page errors — so the bundle ran and the pane rendered; the zero is a measurement.
  positions sidecar:      86 positioned of 459; unpositioned runs 0..13, 27..34, 108..458.

HOW IT WAS FOUND, AND WHY THE JOURNEY EXISTS RATHER THAN THE ENTRY ALONE. Nine journeys were red on this transaction at once. Eight of them went GREEN with the defect untouched: each selects its chain arm as `withSession.filter((t) => t.real)[0]`, `withSession` requires `hasListing`, and four of this chain's rung-3 transactions had NO listing at all because `/aztec-testnet-frames` was published without `just chain-instructions` being run over it. Deriving the missing listings put those four back into the set, `0x00689495…` sorts ahead of `0x0a807e4e…`, and every chain arm moved onto an ordinary instruction-level capture. A corpus that stops covering a defect is indistinguishable from a defect that was fixed, from the verdict line. So the CLASS is named in `corpus.mjs` — `partiallyPositioned`, `stepsPositioned > 0 && stepsUnpositioned > 0`, read from the published `/d/**` facts and not from a page — and journey 27 selects on it. Two subjects today (`aztec-testnet-frames/0x0a807e4e…` and `aztec-testnet/0x20ed5b91…`, which has the same shape at 86 of 108 and whose 22 unpositioned steps are its dispatch prologue), 23 sessions in the complement, so the partition is asserted from both sides.

PROVED ABLE TO FAIL, AND THE SEVEN GREEN RECORDS BESIDE THE THREE RED ONES ARE THE PROOF IT IS NOT VACUOUS: the subject set is non-empty and so is its complement, the class is re-asserted over the numbers it selected on, the SERVED frame marks its position through this same reading, and the live pane put 224 rows on screen. The three that fail are the only three that are about the product.

_comment: Not machine-read. Kept because the both-directions rule paid for itself three times in
two days, and the record is worth more than the lines it costs. Every entry here was
removed because the run FAILED demanding its removal — nobody had to remember.

a-failed-execution-is-tellable-from-a-co.was: The tour's `constraints` program stops on an assertion that cannot hold — 170 against a floor of a million — and its recording ends there. The page presented it identically to a program that ran to completion: both carried the badges 'Succeeded | Synthetic demo data | No timestamp published | Yes | Finalized | Trace ready' and the same provenance sentence, and nothing anywhere said the execution did not finish. A visitor could not tell the two apart without reading the Noir source in the pane.
a-failed-execution-is-tellable-from-a-co.cause: THE FACT WAS NOT PUBLISHED, anywhere. `ExecutionSummary` (src/blocktracer/contract/model.nim) carried steps, frames, truncated, sourceLevel and languages — five keys, none of which is an ending. `truncated` is the nearest neighbour and answers the opposite question: a truncated recording is one whose ending is MISSING. The only place the fact existed was `fixtures/trace/tour/manifest.json`, in the `failure` capability, and the generator read that key only into `g/{gen}/tour.json`, which the transaction and debug routes never open. So no renderer was discarding anything — the contract had no field to discard.
a-failed-execution-is-tellable-from-a-co.closed_by: `ExecutionSummary.ending` — an additive third state (`unstated` / `completed` / `failedConstraint`), omitted from the JSON when unstated so that 'nobody established this' cannot be confused with a claim. The demo generator sets it per tour program from the corpus's own declared capability; `chain/ingest.nim` deliberately leaves every real-chain recording unstated rather than spending the receipt's `revertCode` on it, which is the chain's verdict and the exact conflation the field exists to end. Rendered by `viewutil.executionEndingRow`, added by `txMetadataRows` — the one producer §7.1 requires — so the row reaches both surfaces. Unit-covered by `client/tests/test_capability_tour.nim` suite 3a; mutation arm M in tools/journeys/selftest.mjs.
a-failed-execution-is-tellable-from-a-co.now: The failing recording's page reads 'Stopped on a failed constraint' where the completing one reads 'Ran to completion'. Both still say the TRANSACTION 'Succeeded', which is correct and is the distinction the row exists to make. 9 of 23 published manifests state an ending — the nine tour programs, one failing and eight completing — and the fourteen M5c ones state none.

a-positioned-session-says-where-it-is.was: Six frozen real-chain sessions published a position (step 128 of 235/345/1315) and never said where it was. They correctly stated that the chain publishes no source and that stepping is at instruction level; they never stated the step. The 108 `.srcline` assertions all ran on the demo chain, so this branch had no assertions at all.
a-positioned-session-says-where-it-is.closed_by: 98ccd72 + a490ee3 (`fix/current-line-marker`), landed on dev by a sibling between this branch's first commit and its rebase. `renderPositionHead` now draws 'The session is stopped at step N of M' on the pane that has no line to mark.
a-positioned-session-says-where-it-is.now: 7 of 7 positioned sessions with no line to mark state their step; 13 of 13 positioned sessions say where they are.

position-survives-hydration.was: The hydrated frame marked no line. The served frame showed src/shield.nr with line 32 marked; after hydration the same page showed the same file with 0 lines marked, while the session still published step=128 of 1315. §7.0's 'no state renders less than the pre-hydration page', violated by the product's own bundle.
position-survives-hydration.cause: `decodeSourceIsland` matched the engine's position path against the bundle's document paths with `==`. The engine reports the path the program was RECORDED at — absolute, belonging to the machine that ran it — and the bundle stores paths relative to the package root, because that is the only form that survives being served to someone else. The comparison was false for every file in every session.
position-survives-hydration.why_it_hid: The Nargo.toml fix directly above it made an unmatched position CLEAR currentLine rather than carry it onto the wrong document. Correct — and it turned 'marks the wrong line' into 'marks no line', which is also exactly what a bundle that genuinely lacks the file looks like. The safe fallback masked the broken comparison, and only a browser could tell the two apart.
position-survives-hydration.closed_by: `positionDocumentIndex` in src/debugger/source_island.nim — longest matching path-segment suffix wins. Unit-covered by test_entry_state.nim's eighth suite; mutation arm E in tools/journeys/selftest.mjs.
position-survives-hydration.now: HYDRATED: one line marked, on screen, in the file the position is in — src/main.nr line 1, 'mod shield;'.

stepping-moves-the-position.was: A step advanced the URL and moved nothing on the screen. `?t=` went 1 -> 5 and the recovery anchor went main.nr:12 -> main.nr:13, so the click reached the engine and the engine stepped; `data-step` stayed pinned at its landing value and no line was ever marked.
stepping-moves-the-position.cause: Two causes, and only the first was shared with the entry above. `data-step` was READ once out of the served DOM (`intAttr(ui.root, "data-step")`) and never written again, so the root reported the landing step for the rest of the session. The absent mark was the path-matching defect.
stepping-moves-the-position.why_it_matters_which: Verification-Harness-Traps.md §2 in the product rather than in a harness: every success along the way was real. A check written against `location.search` would have been green throughout, which is why journey 03 reads the URL as a CONTROL and takes its verdict from the rendered position.
stepping-moves-the-position.closed_by: `renderPanes` now writes `data-step` and `data-total-steps` on every re-render — in the proc that draws the panes, so the attribute and the panes cannot disagree. Mutation arm F.
stepping-moves-the-position.now: data-step 0 -> 1 (of 1315), marked line 1 -> 12, exactly one mark after the step.

renderSource-stack-overflow-on-a-multi-m.was: On the FeeJuice transaction — `aztec-testnet/0x20ed5b91…`, the busiest page in the corpus and the one the product is demonstrated on — the live panes never painted. `renderSource` threw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` on its 4,082,980-byte document, the exception unwound out of `renderPanes` before the call-trace pane was written, and everything interactive on that page was unavailable. Seven uncaught page errors per plain load; 24 under journey 25, which clicks six rows and re-renders. The STATIC page was correct throughout — 81 `ctrow`, 2 `ctfold`, 44 `ctline` — which is why no DOM assertion anywhere noticed.
renderSource-stack-overflow-on-a-multi-m.cause: ARGUMENT-COUNT EXHAUSTION, NOT RECURSION DEPTH — and this entry exists partly to correct the record, because the previous ledger text blamed `Array.prototype.concat`, which is the SAFE operation and would have sent the next reader in the wrong direction. Nothing was recursing: the failing stack has ONE `renderSource` frame. Nim's JS backend represents `string` as an array of char codes and compiles `dest.add(src)` to `dest.push.apply(dest, src)`, which passes every character of `src` as a separate ARGUMENT; engines cap that at roughly 65k–125k. `debugger.nim` appended whole rendered subtrees that way — a document panel, a layout subtree, a folded call-trace group — so the append blew as soon as a panel got large. Measured directly with `nim js` 2.2.4 on a standalone probe: `push.apply` and `strutils.join` both throw at 4 MB; `&` compiles to `concat`, takes the operand as ONE argument, and is safe past 5 MB.
renderSource-stack-overflow-on-a-multi-m.fix:
`debugger.nim:addHtml` — `&` on the JS backend, `add` on the native one — applied to the five sites whose operand is a whole rendered subtree, and deliberately NOT to the per-row loops, where in-place append is what keeps rendering linear. The served page is byte-identical afterwards.

AND THE GATE, which is the more important half: seven uncaught errors per load went unnoticed indefinitely because `pageErrors` was collected by `visit`, returned, and asserted by only four of thirty-one journeys. It is now wired into the act of loading a page — `probe.mjs:UNCAUGHT` records every uncaught exception with its stack, and `run.mjs` fails the run over it, grouped per page, naming the count and printing the first stack.

a-call-trace-row-lands-on-the-frame-it-n.was: ONE assertion was red: '…and each of those frames states a DIFFERENT source position — counted 1, the claim says 6'. Six rows sharing a coordinate were clicked; the marked row moved correctly six times and every one of the six reported the same position, `fee_juice_contract/src/main.nr:148`.
a-call-trace-row-lands-on-the-frame-it-n.cause:
THE ASSERTION, not the product — and the entry that stood here named a defect in the wrong repository.

ITS LEADING SUSPECT IS REFUTED. It read: codetracer's `dap_handler.calltrace_jump` takes its request as `_req` and never responds, so the position waits on an answer that never comes. BlockTracer NEVER SENDS `ct/calltrace-jump`. `hydrate.rowHandler` is `selectCalltraceFrame` plus `ct/goto-ticks`, which is what `Click-Navigation.md` §4 specifies for a hydrated page ("the seek is `ct/goto-ticks` in BlockTracer … and `ct/calltrace-jump` in CodeTracer"). That command is not on this product's path at any rung. It was also already fixed upstream, on codetracer `dev`, with the response added and the same omission found and fixed in `event_jump` beside it.

WHAT THE ASSERTION ACTUALLY MEASURED, and it is a real reading: the live pane gives every frame the location of the tick it starts at, so the six frames that share one tick share one location, while the static export gives the same six `map.nr:36 / map.nr:11 / hash.nr:221 / hash.nr:212 / poseidon2.nr:16 / poseidon2.nr:68` because it numbers a frame from the callee's first step. Two producers, two honest readings of "the coordinate a frame starts at" — the open question `session_project.projectCalltrace` records as #234.

AND THE SPEC SAYS THAT IS NOT A DEFECT. `Click-Navigation.md` §2.2 states it as the premise the whole section is built on: "in a real recording many frames share one coordinate, and several functions in several different files can all resolve to a single call site". §2.3 adds the rule directly — "a check written for this document must not assert a coordinate's value" — and sends the choice of convention to `Trace-Artifacts.md` rather than making it. So the assertion required an unmade decision to have gone one way. It was also redundant: the record above it already establishes that six clicks mark six different FRAMES, by identity.

PROPOSED, for `Trace-Artifacts.md` — where `Click-Navigation.md` §2.3 sends the decision it declines to make — because the disagreement it blesses has a visible cost this journey measured:

A producer that reports the call site instead gives every frame in a chain of immediate calls the CALLER's position, so a row naming one function displays another function's file and line — and where the outer frames are bytecode, a source-level frame is labelled with the bytecode pseudo-file."

a-link-to-a-frame-arrives-at-that-frame.cause:
THE LIVE CALL TRACE MARKED NOTHING UNTIL SOMETHING SELECTED A FRAME. `session_project.projectCalltrace` renders `current: vm.selectedEntry.val == some(line.index)` — a SELECTION — and the only writer of `selectedEntry` was `selectCalltraceFrame`, which runs on a CLICK. On a landing nothing has clicked, so the comparison was against `none` for every row.

MEASURED, served against hydrated on one page: 47 served rows with exactly one `ctrow … cur`, and one second later 48 hydrated rows with none. So hydration REMOVED a fact the visitor already had, which is `Page-Descriptions.md` §7.0 exactly — "No state renders less than the pre-hydration page" — violated in the one direction that clause exists to forbid. It also silently undid `hydrate.markServedFrame`: a §6.0a link marked the served row and the first live render threw the mark away, which is why three of six links appeared to work — a race, not a feature.

It hid because `renderSource` used to overflow the JavaScript stack on this capture's 4 MB document and unwound out of `renderPanes` BEFORE the call-trace pane was written, so the pane kept the static export's markup and the journey read the served page's answer through a dead hydration. Fixing the overflow turned a false green into a true red.
a-link-to-a-frame-arrives-at-that-frame.closed_by: `session_project.selectLandingFrame` plus one call site in `hydrate.paint`, gated by `Hydration.frameSeeded` to the first live render that has rows. It writes the pointer rather than teaching a second reader to guess at it — which is the shape codetracer `1dcf2e0ea` fixed the same night on `showTab`. Which frame a landing selects is §6.0a's own precedence and no new rule: the frame the LINK named, when it named one this window holds, and otherwise the frame the SESSION is stopped in, by the relation `session_view.selectionDetail` already states — "the frame containing the position is the last one that started at or before it". The link's frame is carried across as its `call:` ANCHOR and not as an index, because the two row lists are different lengths (47 served, 48 live) and `Click-Navigation.md` §4 requires the identity to be the thing that survives.
a-link-to-a-frame-arrives-at-that-frame.now:
GREEN, 14 of 14 — and DETERMINISTICALLY, which the line that stood here could not say. It read "GREEN, 10 of 10", and that was one sample of a distribution reported as a proof.

RE-MEASURED BEFORE ANY CHANGE, 20 runs of this journey on one unchanged tree at 779c702: 14 RED and 6 green. So the entry was removed from `known_red` on an observation that comes up about three times in ten, and for the rest of the time `dev` carried a red journey with no entry naming it. The defect this entry closes really is closed — that part was right, and it is re-proved below — but the evidence offered for it was a green, and a green is not a claim about determinism.

WHAT ACTUALLY VARIED WAS THE JOURNEY, NOT THE PRODUCT, and the 20 runs separate the two cleanly. Every identity assertion was 6 of 6 on all 20 runs: each link left exactly one row marked, it was the row that link NAMED, the six marked six different rows, and every one moved the mark off the unlinked page's row. A visitor clicking the same link twice arrives at the same frame. What moved was the journey's reading of it:

  subject step        58 on 12 runs, 59 on 8      <- the SUBJECT itself moved
  control row         [1] enqueued-call-0 on 12, [45] avm_return on 8
  "different source position"   1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 — every value in range

THE MECHANISM. The journey settled on `phase !== "fetching"` and read once. Measured on the built site, `fetching` is the SERVED page's own phase, so that predicate does not hold the page before the engine — it WAITS for the engine and releases at `opening`, 0.2-0.3 s. Hydration repaints the Call Trace pane from the live producer at 2.3-2.7 s. The read therefore fell in a 2 s gap it had no reason to win, and the journey makes EIGHT such reads which raced independently. The two producers number the same session differently — 47 served rows against 48 live, step 59 against step 58, and a frame's location taken from the callee's own first step against the tick's location — so a read that drifted answered a different question in the same shape. The last count was a MIXTURE: k reads on the served rows contribute k distinct positions and the rest all contribute `main.nr:148`, which is why every value from 1 to 6 appears.

FIXED BY PINNING THE READ, not by retrying it. The engine is now HELD IN FLIGHT (`probe.visit` gained `holdRoutes`), which turns the interval §6.3 is about into a state with no deadline to beat; the six links settle on `#dbg-position-notice`, the product's own sentence about the landing, which is positive and monotone; and a new assertion reads `tagName === "A"` on every row of all seven pre-engine reads, so WHOSE rows were counted is now a fact the run states rather than one it assumed. The subject is pinned too: the served rows give six frames to step 59 AND six to step 92, so "the biggest group" named two things and `[0]` took whichever the Map held first — the comparator is now total (size, then the smaller step), as is the one that orders candidate transactions.

AND THE HYDRATED SIDE IS STILL JUDGED, which pinning nearly cost. Pinning every read to the pre-engine state made selftest arm FJ3 SURVIVE, measured: the arm reconstructs the §7.0 defect this entry closes, and it had only ever been killed because the reads sometimes landed on the hydrated pane BY ACCIDENT. Coverage that rests on a race is not coverage. Journey 26 now visits each of the six links a second time with the engine let through, waits for the producer to change rather than for a phase, and asserts the repainted pane still marks exactly one row and that it is still the frame the link named, carried across by anchor. FJ3 is re-aimed at that assertion and is KILLED again (counted 0, the claim says 6); a new arm FJ4 drops the anchor at the hydration seam and is killed by the carry-across assertion.

PROVED ON THE FIX: 20 further runs on one unchanged tree, 20 green, 14 of 14 every time, one subject (step 59) and one control row ([45] avm_return) on all 20 — every column of the distribution single-valued, where before every one of them had moved. Re-measured 5 more times after rebasing onto 788fb5d, identical. And the four mutation arms aimed at this journey all kill on that base: FJ1 and FJ2 on the pre-engine reads, FJ3 re-aimed at §7.0's floor, and FJ4 new for the anchor carry-across.
a-link-to-a-frame-arrives-at-that-frame.still_open: WHAT A TOOLBAR STEP DOES TO THE MARK. `Click-Navigation.md` §3.3 says "before anything has been chosen, no row is marked" and §5 reads it as "on a freshly loaded session, assert the count of marked rows is zero" — which contradicts §7.0's floor here, because the served page marks one and hydration may not render less. The two are reconcilable only by separating the frame the session IS IN from the frame a visitor CHOSE; BlockTracer's `.cur` is currently the union of both. The seed is written once, on the landing, so a step afterwards leaves the mark where it was rather than re-deriving it — deliberately, because re-deriving would send all six frames sharing one coordinate back to the innermost of them. Naming the two states is a spec change and is proposed rather than made here.
a-link-to-a-frame-arrives-at-that-frame.proposed_clause:
PROPOSED, for `Click-Navigation.md` §3.3, replacing "Before anything has been chosen, no row is marked." — because as written it contradicts `Page-Descriptions.md` §7.0 on this product, whose landing is positioned and whose served page marks the frame it is positioned in:

  "A row is marked whenever the session is in a frame the pane is showing. The mark answers 'where am I', so a positioned session marks exactly one row from the moment it is positioned, and a session that is not positioned marks none. 'Nothing is positioned yet' and 'you are in this frame' are different states and must look different.

  An activation chooses WHICH row the mark names when the coordinate cannot. Several frames share one coordinate (§2.2), so 'the frame the session is in' is not always a single row; an activation says which of the tied rows the visitor meant."

with §5's reading amended to: on a freshly loaded POSITIONED session the count of marked rows is one and on an unpositioned one it is zero; then activate a row that shares its coordinate with another and assert the count is still one and it is the row activated.
a-link-to-a-frame-arrives-at-that-frame.evidence_rule: A JOURNEY'S VERDICT IS A SAMPLE UNTIL A DISTRIBUTION SAYS OTHERWISE. This entry was retired on "GREEN, 10 of 10" while the journey was red 14 times in 20, and nothing in the record could have revealed that, because ten greens and a coin that lands green three times in ten are written down identically. The reading that would have caught it costs one loop: run the journey 20 times on an unchanged tree and report the DISTRIBUTION of what it measured — the subject it chose, the row it called the control, the counts it produced — not the number of times it passed. Where a journey reads a page that is still changing, it must also assert WHICH state it read; journey 26's flap was invisible for exactly as long as nothing checked whose rows were being counted.
